name: Trusts Issuer
description: A principal registers trust in an OIDC issuer — its configured issuer URL matches the issuer's canonical host. A generic federation relationship, not specific to any one cloud: an AWS IAM OIDC provider, a GCP workload-identity pool, an Azure federated credential, or a Kubernetes/Vault JWT trust are all sources. The source is WILDCARD (omitted) precisely so any principal type can trust an issuer without identity_core depending upward on that principal's plugin — the substrate owns the generic vocabulary, the domain plugin supplies the source node. Owning this edge TYPE asserts no trust (existence != trust); a trust instance exists only when an emitter creates the edge. In v0 the only emitter is github_core's enrichment, matching aws_iam_oidc_provider.url against the issuer host. Derived link (not hotlink-backed): the provider is written by aws_core, which neither knows about nor emits this edge.

link_rule.description: Derived-link provenance: the name of the declarative grid-link manifest rule that emitted this edge (WHICH rule matched). Written by enrichment engines (v0: github_core's); comes paired with matched_value or not at all. The same provenance shape rides every manifest-derived edge type — if the derived-link engine ever graduates to a substrate, these keys become a system-owned lane (see req-grid-edge-schema-required-5 in core's spec-grid-edge.md).

matched_value.description: Derived-link provenance: the exact value the rule matched on (e.g. the issuer host) — WHAT the derivation keyed on.
